source_excerpt:
Native ComfyUI support for Idol , Speridlabs' single image to 3D gaussian splat model: one picture of an object in, a 3DGS splat (with the unseen sides) out, in a few seconds on a modern GPU.
No requirements. Pure ComfyUI. Nothing is installed, no model code is shipped.
Stock nodes. Idol is the TripoSplat architecture retrained, and ComfyUI implements that natively, so the weights load with Load Diffusion Model and Load VAE and the stock TripoSplat nodes, KSampler, Render Splat, Save Splat and the 3D viewer run it. ComfyUI's offloading, dtypes, attention backends and torch.compile apply as usual.
Three small nodes for what Idol's pipeline adds on top: Idol Preprocess Image (its synthetic / real crop modes, background removal in place), Idol Camera (the camera Idol predicts for the input, to re-render the input view or start a turntable from it) and Idol Prune Splat (drops the near-transparent gaussians that make the viewer and exports look hazy).
Clone into ComfyUI/custom_nodes and restart ComfyUI:
Needs a ComfyUI with TripoSplat support (0.22 or newer).
The first two are Idol's own weights (the denoiser, and the octree + gaussian decoders) in ComfyUI's file layout, made with scripts/convert.py . The other three are the same encoders Idol uses: DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 and the FLUX.2 VAE condition the denoiser, BiRefNet cuts the object out. If you already run TripoSplat in ComfyUI you have them.
Drag example_workflows/idol_image_to_splat.json into ComfyUI, or open it from Templates → Custom Nodes → ComfyUI-Idol . It is the standard TripoSplat graph with the Idol files and the two Idol nodes:
Those KSampler values are Idol's defaults. Its cfg_strength 3.0 is (1 + w) * cond - w * uncond , which is ComfyUI cfg 4.0 ; its time shift rescale_t 3.0 is the model's sampling shift and already in the model config, so no ModelSamplingSD3 node is needed; its 50 Euler steps on linspace(1, 0) are exactly euler / simple . dpmpp_2m at 20 steps (the TripoSplat template's setting) is a faster trade-off.
Crop mode matters. Idol was trained with the object spanning 1/1.2 of the frame for renders and generated images ( synthetic ) and 1/1.7 for photographs ( real ). custom sets the margin directly.
Photographs: mode real , a clean cutout (BiRefNet does well on a single object against a simple background; for hard cases paint the mask yourself and connect it), the object centred and whole in the frame, and the reference's sampling (50 steps, cfg 4). The model was trained on single objects, so crop out neighbours and supports. Nothing else in the graph is photo-specific.
Haze, spikes and fuzzy edges in the 3D viewer or an export are the near-transparent gaussians: Idol emits about half of its gaussians with opacity under 0.05, and viewers draw all of them. The reference SDK's own .ply of the same image has the same halo (rendered side by side they are indistinguishable), so this is the model as released, not the port. Idol Prune Splat removes them ( min_opacity 0.05; max_scale 0.05 also cuts needle-shaped spikes at the silhouette) and halves the file; Render Splat and Extract Mesh have the same threshold built in ( opacity_threshold , min_opacity ). It changes what the result looks like far more than any sampler setting.
Transparent PNGs: Idol uses an image's own alpha when it has one. In ComfyUI, Load Image's mask is the transparent region, so pass it through Invert Mask into Idol Preprocess Image's mask ; the background removal model is then not needed.
Check the result from the input view. Idol predicts the camera the input was taken from. Render Splat with Idol Camera's camera_info gives that view; if it does not resemble the preprocessed image something went wrong upstream (usually the mask or the crop mode).
Density: 262144 gaussians matches the octree's point density. Higher values (up to 1048576) oversample the same points, so they are denser but add no detail and cost VRAM and time; 65536 is a fast preview.
Live preview: the stock TripoSplat Sampling Preview node (in the workflow) shows a coarse decode at every step. Bypass it to save a little time.
Speed: cond and uncond are batched, attention goes through ComfyUI's optimized attention, and the trunk runs in fp16 like the reference: on an RTX 5090 the 50 Euler steps take about 18 s and the 262144 gaussian decode 4 to 8 s, without compilation. TorchCompileModel on the diffusion model works; the first run compiles. The decode scales with num_gaussians .
Exports: Save Splat / Create 3D File write .ply (full 3DGS), .spz and .ksplat . The .ply is the same convention as Idol's own save_ply (y-up, degree-0 SH, log scale, logit opacity), so it opens in any splat viewer. Extract Mesh from Splat gives a GLB.
Idol Preprocess Image : IMAGE (+ MASK or BACKGROUND_REMOVAL) → IMAGE, MASK
What idol.preprocess does, on tensors: the short side is resized to 1024, the object's alpha (your mask, or BiRefNet's prediction when none is connected) is eroded by erode_radius pixels so no background fringe survives, a square of mode × the object's bounding box is cropped around it, resized to size × size and composited on black. The mask output is the alpha in that frame.
Idol Prune Splat : SPLAT → SPLAT, count
Drops gaussians with opacity below min_opacity and, if max_scale is set, those whose longest axis exceeds it (object units; the object spans about one). Batches keep per-item counts. Put it between TripoSplat Decode and anything that saves, previews or renders.
Idol Camera : LATENT → LOAD3D_CAMERA, yaw, pitch, distance, fov
The denoiser denoises a 5-value camera token next to the object latent (direction, inverse distance, half-width). This node decodes it from the KSampler output into a camera_info for Render Splat, Create Camera Info and the 3D previews, plus yaw / pitch (degrees, Create Camera Info's orbit convention: yaw here is 180° minus Idol's yaw, pitch is the same), distance and vertical fov. Orthographic predictions become a far perspective camera (distance 1000), like the reference.
Idol's released files are the TripoSplat networks under their original parameter names, so the conversion is only a file layout change:
denoiser.safetensors → diffusion_models/idol_fp16.safetensors . The only key ComfyUI does not expect is pos_pe , the latent tokens' fixed Sobol positions; ComfyUI recomputes that buffer ( SobolEngine , seed 123) and the script checks the stored one is identical before dropping it. The original fp32 file also loads directly (with an "unexpected key" warning).
decoder.safetensors + decoder_gs.safetensors → vae/idol_decoder_fp16.safetensors , one file with the octree. and gs. prefixes ComfyUI's TripoSplat gaussian decoder is detected by. The gaussian representation config Idol ships (32 gaussians per anchor, softplus scaling with bias 0.004, opacity bias 0.1, 0.0009 filter kernel, perturbation 1.5) is exactly ComfyUI's default for that decoder.
birefnet.safetensors is Comfy-Org's BiRefNet without its training heads, so the stock file is used.
fp16 is the precision the reference runs the transformer trunks at; --dtype bf16 and fp32 also work.
tests/parity.py checks the ComfyUI path against the reference implementation ( idol-sdk ) on random inputs: the denoiser's velocity for the latent and the camera, the octree decoder's logits, the gaussian decoder's activated gaussians and the PLY frame transform, the preprocessing and the camera decode. From the released fp32 weights the denoiser matches to 3e-6 relative error and the decoders to ~1e-4 to 3e-3 (ComfyUI's fused RMSNorm uses eps 1e-6 where the reference normalizes with none; with eps 0 they match exactly); the fp16 files add ~1e-3.
tests/e2e.py runs the whole graph headless through the stock node classes and writes the .ply , the preprocessed input, the render from the predicted camera and a turntable sheet.
Idol is by Speridlabs (Apache-2.0). It is the TripoSplat architecture by VAST-AI-Research, whose ComfyUI implementation runs it here. Image encoders: DINOv3 (Meta) and the FLUX.2 VAE (Black Forest Labs); background removal: BiRefNet (Zheng et al.). Each has its own license. This pack is Apache-2.0; see NOTICE.
